title: Compact Rulebook Dispatch Transcoder — Draft
content:
Purpose: quick personal sketch for a small component that converts a high-level routing rulebook (human-friendly DSL + attributes) into a compact, runtime-efficient dispatch table and telemetry mapping suitable for the ingress layer.

Motivation:
- Current rulebooks are expressive but expensive to evaluate per-request (regexes, nested conditions, poly-match operations).
- We need a translator that produces a compact dispatch artifact (byte-efficient, predictable eval cost) for fast path lookups in the ingress plane.
- Keep source rulebooks editable by SRE/product, but produce artifacts pinned to model versions & rollout policies.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Deterministic per-request eval steps (max N probes).
- Small serialized footprint (target < 6KB per rulebook for small tenants).
- Backward-compatible decoders across runtime releases.
- Include telemetry mapping hooks (span names, tags) so ingress emits useful signals without runtime recomputation.

High-level flow (ascii):

  +-------------+    rulebook.dsl   +----------------+    compact.artifact    +--------------+
  | Human edit  | -----------------> | Transcoder CLI | ---------------------> | Ingress DSPR |
  | (web/edit)  |                    | (server-side)  |                       | (fast eval)  |
  +-------------+                     +----------------+                       +--------------+

Transcoder responsibilities:
- Parse DSL -> AST. Validate semantics (no cycles, fallback present).
- Normalize predicates (tokenize, canonicalize host/path/headers/feature flags).
- Produce a compact decision graph: node table + edge table + literal pool.
- Produce a telemetry map: node_id -> {span_name, metric_tags[]}.
- Attach metadata: source hash, compiler version, compatibility header.

Example DSL snippet (informal):
  rulebook "tenant-alpha" {
    default -> variant(bert-7b-q2a);
    if header.X-Region == "eu" and path starts_with "/checkout" -> variant(bert-7b-q2a, latency_hint=10ms);
    if session.user_tier == "enterprise" -> route pool:reserved-high;
    if attr.prompt_len > 2048 -> fallback variant(adaptive-low-latency);
  }

Rough target artifact shape (conceptual, will be compacted and binary-encoded):
- header: {version: 1, compiler: "transcoder-v0.3", src_hash: "sha256:..."}
- literals: ["/checkout","eu","X-Region","session.user_tier","enterprise"]
- nodes: [
    {id:0, type:match, op:hdr_eq, literal_idx:2, yes:1, no:4},
    {id:1, type:match, op:path_prefix, literal_idx:0, yes:2, no:3},
    {id:2, type:action, action:bind_variant, variant_id:5, telemetry: {span:"ingress.route.checkout_eu", tags:["region:eu"]}},
    ...
  ]
- variants table: [ {id:5, model:"bert-7b-q2a",quant:"q2a"}, ... ]

Compression notes:
- Intern literal pool and use small integer indices (u16) everywhere.
- Node table as flat arrays: op_code, arg, yes_idx, no_idx to avoid nested structures.
- Use RLE or varint for dense sequences.
- Optionally precompute hot-path jump table (for simple header match + prefix combos).

Ingress runtime eval pseudocode (fast path):
- load artifact -> memory map (shared mem)
- while node != ACTION:
    switch(op_code[node]){
      case HDR_EQ: v = lookup_header(literals[arg]); node = v ? yes_idx : no_idx; break;
      case PATH_PREFIX: v = path_starts_with(literals[arg]); node = v ? yes_idx : no_idx; break;
      case ATTR_GT: v = get_attr(arg) > literal_val; node = ...; break;
    }
- perform action (route to pool / bind variant).

Telemetry mapping:
- Attach telemetry to nodes: when taking edge X emit metric counter metric_name + tags.
- Emit sparse sample on fallback branches so we can surface bad rulebook coverage.
- Export a compact telemetry table that maps node_id->(span, metric_key, tags_idx) where tags_idx references same literal pool.

Versioning and compatibility:
- Header includes schema_version and compiler_semver.
- Runtime must accept older (downgrade) and newer (graceful degrade) artifacts. Strategy: runtime supports a small set of op_codes; transcoder can compile complex ops into micrographs of supported ops.
- Keep feature flags for experimental ops (e.g., fuzzy string match).

Safety/fallthrough:
- Ensure every rulebook has an explicit default action. Transcoder must reject rulebooks without explicit default.
- Provide a "safe-mode" compile that limits actions to read-only routing (no autop-run of canary toggles).

Mini API spec for transcoder service (sketch):
- POST /compile (multipart) -> body: { rulebook_dsl: text, target_schema: "ingress-v1", constraints: {max_nodes: 1024, max_literals: 256}}
  returns: 202 accepted -> job_id
- GET /compile/{job_id} -> { status: queued|ok|err, artifact_url: s3://..., warnings: [...] }
- GET /artifact/{artifact_id} -> binary blob (or base64 encoded in JSON)

Operational concerns and heuristics:
- Build artifact differencing: on compile, produce a human diff (AST -> minimized change set) so SREs can review.
- Hot-reload safety: use versioned artifact keys, staged rollout (canary percentage). Ingress nodes should keep old and new artifact for a grace period to ensure no in-flight mismatches.
- Size guardrails: if artifact > threshold -> fail compile unless override flag provided.
- Cost analysis: compute an estimated per-request eval cost (#ops on hot path) and include in compile warnings.

Open questions / TODOs (brain-dump):
- How to handle dynamic tenant attributes (session.*) that are only available after auth? Do we allow split-stage evaluation (pre-auth fast pass + post-auth refine)?
- Support for lists/sets: rulebooks often say "if header in [a,b,c]". Compiler can expand into multiple HDR_EQ nodes or add a bloom filter op. Bloom filter has false positives — acceptable? Need SLO discussion.
- Telemetry volume: attaching metrics to lots of nodes could be noisy. Need sampling strategy plus tag cardinality limits.
- Encoding: prefer CBOR for compactness + easier typed binary. But current infra prefers protobufs. Maybe produce both: raw proto + compressed CBOR payload.
- Local testing harness: small CLI to emulate ingress lookup with sample requests and produce per-request op trace. High priority.

Notes to self for next steps:
- Prototype translator as Rust binary (fast, good binary encoding libs).
- Implement a minimal op set: HDR_EQ, PATH_PREFIX, ATTR_GT, ATTR_LT, CONST_TRUE, ACTION_BIND_VARIANT, ACTION_ROUTE_POOL. Keep it tiny.
- Add unit tests: adversarial rulebooks that try to exceed node/literal limits.
- Build a small web preview: upload DSL -> visualize decision graph + estimated cost. Useful for product and SRE review.

Related artifacts I should reference when iterating:
- RD-1423 ingress rulebook proposal (TODO: pull exact examples)
- telemetry-span-naming-guidelines (confluence)

End of sketch. This is intentionally rough — mostly a checklist and shape notes for a small compiler/transcoder that reduces expressive rulebooks into deterministic, compact dispatch tables for the ingress fast path.

-- Jordan
